content.text:
The pattern is best explained by Ti8BiO7 (mp-1105121) alone.

- **Strongest peaks.** The two strongest low-angle peaks are at 12.4° (d ≈ 7.13 Å) and 10.45° (d ≈ 8.46 Å).
  - From the cell (a = b = 9.337 Å, γ = 130.2°), the primitive (100) spacing is a·sin γ ≈ 7.13 Å, which matches 12.4°.
  - In the C-centred conventional cell (≈16.94 × 7.86 Å), (200) gives d ≈ 8.47 Å, which matches 10.45°.
  - The conventional (110) also gives 7.13 Å, consistent with 12.4° being the strongest line.
- **Higher-angle peaks.** With c = 3.037 Å, the hk1 reflections fall at about 31.3° (201) and 32.0° (111). These roughly match the observed pair near 31.0° and 31.7°.
  - The ~38.6° peak is only loosely matched, by (221) predicted near 38.9°.
  - I did not index the other mid-angle peaks (39.95°, 43.7°, 46.3°, 47.2°).
- **Alternatives.** BaCaSmSbO6 has c = 8.47 Å, so its (001) would sit at 10.45°. However, it does not account for the dominant 12.4° line. Cs2Ti(WO4)3 would put its first strong line near 14.7°, which is not observed. I did not check the other candidates in detail.

I found no peak that clearly requires a second phase, but since not every line was indexed, confidence is moderate.

{"present": ["mp-1105121"], "confidence": 0.7, "note": "The strongest peaks at 12.4 and 10.45 degrees index to Ti8BiO7 (d = 7.13 and 8.47 Å), with hk1 lines near 31-32 degrees roughly matching and no second phase clearly needed, though several mid-angle peaks were not indexed."}
